ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and signatories against the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Unit (EMLTU) sanctions list, United Nations Security Council sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and domestic designations by the Egyptian Terrorism Entities List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring; failure to screen is a criminal offense under the AML Law and CBE regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Electronic Services Portal and Commercial Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed Arabic trade name is mandatory for domestic use and must be distinguishable from existing registered names in the Commercial Registry. The name may also be rendered in English/Latin script for cross-border SaaS branding; where the proposed name is in a foreign language, an Arabic transliteration and a meaning declaration must be filed with the commercial registrar. Names that are misleading, contrary to public order, or identical to a pre-existing trademark/company name are rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of rejection, the applicant or its local attorney may submit a written administrative complaint to the GAFI Corporate Services Directorate within 30 days from the date of rejection, attaching the original name reservation application, a legal memorandum establishing non-conflict and non-prohibited use, and any supporting trademark-search results. GAFI must issue a decision within 15 working days. An unsuccessful administrative remedy may be appealed to the Administrative Court of the Council of State within 60 days from notification of the second refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as a standalone registered office for Egyptian LLC incorporation. A physical address in Egypt is mandatory for service of process and tax notification. Serviced offices / executive suites that provide a dedicated meeting room and a fixed physical reception may satisfy the GAFI requirement; pure 'virtual office' post-box arrangements are rejected. For B2B SaaS enterprises, the registered office may be an administrative office, provided it is not solely a residential address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual likelihood for a low-risk B2B SaaS business; probability increases to 25% if future banking, payment-processing, or government-contract activities are added.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Law No. 5 of 2022; LLC formation, capital, management, and registration provisions (Articles 1, 4, 7, 10-15, 26-35); read with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree 2310/2017).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) One-Stop Shop, in coordination with the Commercial Registry (Qism Al-Tuguari) under the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contract of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Aqd Ta'sis wa Al-Nizam Al-Dakhili) registered in the Commercial Registry (Qayd Al-Sijil Al-Tijari).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Law No. 159/1981; subscribed capital must be fully paid in cash deposited to a bank account in the company's name or in-kind appraised by an accredited evaluator. No statutory escrow of capital is required; the GAFI clearance requires submission of the bank certificate of deposit at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation contract and the subscribed capital distribution set forth in the Memorandum of Association are ratified, and the Founders' subscription to the issued shares is approved, with paid-up capital to be deposited in the company's bank account. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be located at the address specified in the incorporation contract and lease agreement, effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [NAME A] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [NAME B] is appointed Company Secretary, with authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and represent the company before GAFI, tax authorities, and regulators. RESOLVED further, that Officers may delegate operational matters to employees and advisors, all to be recorded in these minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Business Object Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop and Commercial Registry name database (digital submission via GAFI portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three alternative Arabic names with English transliteration for the reserved LLC trade name; the authority runs a conflict check against the Commercial Registry and trademark registers. Include a business object clause covering 'enterprise cloud software applications development and B2B SaaS subscriptions (ISIC 6201)' so that the registered scope covers subscription, hosting, and consulting services.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application with three alternatives
Passport or national ID copies of all shareholders
Notarized power of attorney if submitted by a licensed agent
Declared business object clause (Arabic, ISIC 6201 wording)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing trademark or registered company, file a written justification with the Ministry of Trade and Industry naming committee and re-submit a revised priority list of names within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Authority (Al-Tawthiq) and GAFI Legal Affairs Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the incorporation contract (Aqd Ta'sis) and Articles of Association in Arabic with English translation; all founders must appear physically before the notary, submit tax-identification evidence if Egyptian residents, and remit notarial stamp duties. The GAFI legal reviewer verifies mandatory clauses: company name, object, capital distribution, manager appointment, and dispute resolution under Law 159/1981.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation contract and Articles of Association (bilingual)
Name reservation certificate
Passport and national ID copies of shareholders and managers
Registered office lease intention letter or title abstract
AML and source-of-funds declarations for foreign shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or GAFI raises legal comments, adopt a supplementary founders' decision amending the relevant clause, re-notarize the supplemental memorandum, and resubmit the consolidated text to GAFI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-Up Capital Deposit and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian-licensed commercial bank (opening account in the LLC's reserved name)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account under the reserved company name and deposit the full subscribed paid-up capital; request a bank certificate of deposit issued to GAFI. For in-kind capital contributions, obtain an appraisal by an accredited valuer registered with the Egyptian Authority for Financial Supervision.
required_dossiers: Provisional account opening forms
Draft incorporation contract
Passports/IDs of authorized signatories
Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds evidence
Name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML/KYC queries, provide enhanced source-of-funds declarations and a banker's reference; if the file is still declined, select an alternative licensed bank and complete the same procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI One-Stop Shop Filing and Company Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Cairo central office or provincial subsidiary; electronic upload plus physical counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the consolidated dossier to the GAFI One-Stop Shop, pay the official registration and publication fees, and receive the certificate of incorporation. GAFI simultaneously forwards the company record to the Commercial Registry for the automatic commercial register entry (Qayd Al-Sijil Al-Tijari).
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Name reservation certificate
Registered office lease contract or title deed
Passport photographs and ID copies of managers
Completed GAFI application form and fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is queried, cure with a supplementary statement and resubmit missing evidence within the statutory objection window; if GAFI exceeds the deadline, invoke the deemed-registration provision by filing a formal demand with GAFI's legal complaints unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Entry, Tax Card, and VAT Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry) and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI issuance, complete the Commercial Registry entry and obtain the registry excerpt; open the tax file at the ETA and obtain the Tax Card (Basita Dharibiya). If annual taxable supplies of the SaaS subscription operations exceed EGP 500,000, register for VAT simultaneously via the ETA portal.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial Registry entry form
Bank certificate of deposit and lease contract
Tax declaration forms and authorized signatory ID
Certified copy of board resolution appointing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA returns the file for missing formalities, appear at the competent tax office with corrected forms and obtain a certificate of pending tax-card issuance; appeal any rejection through the ETA internal contestation procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Insurance, Municipal Office Licensing, and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), District Municipality (Hayy), and Civil Defense Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer with NOSI within 30 days of first hiring; submit the lease and floor plan to the district municipality for the office establishment permit (Mahall license); arrange for the Civil Defense fire-safety inspection and obtain a clearance certificate for the premises.
required_dossiers: Tax Card and incorporation certificate
Lease contract with approved land-use classification
Building floor plan and structural safety statement
Civil defense inspection application and fire-fighting equipment list
Employee contracts and NOSI registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For fire-safety queries, install required fire-extinguishing and exit-signage upgrades and obtain a re-inspection report; for municipal objections, provide a registered engineer's structural clearance and appeal to the municipal licensing committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 (enterprise cloud software) is a non-industrial digital service; Industrial Development Authority facility licensing is not triggered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required; the GAFI incorporation certificate, Commercial Registry entry, Tax Card, and Civil Defense fire-safety approval together constitute the operating authorization for the registered office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 service occupation with no industrial installation; no environmental development file or EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no regulated wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams; general waste segregation and e-waste disposal obligations under Environmental Law No. 4/1994 apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Law No. 43/1979 fire-safety certificate for the registered office; building structural safety clearance endorsed by a registered engineer; workplace occupational health clearance under Labor Law No. 12/2003.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg (for VAT/e-invoicing), and the Egyptian Taxpayers Registration System accessible via the ETA's online services; for customs, the Egypt Customs Authority (ECA) under the Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an Egyptian LLC must obtain: (1) a Commercial Registration certificate from the Commercial Registry; (2) a tax card (TIN) from the Egyptian Tax Authority; (3) a VAT registration certificate (Value Added Tax ID) if taxable supplies exceed the statutory registration threshold or if the entity is a direct exporter; (4) a file number for withholding tax purposes. For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment, registration for VAT and withholding tax may be required only where a direct taxable supply or e-commerce nexus exists. The ETA requires submission of the company incorporation documents, lease/ownership proof of premises, passport copies of managers, and bank account opening certificate. Registration can be completed online through the ETA portal or in person at the relevant tax office. The LLC's TIN (Tax Identification Number) is issued without minimum capital requirement; a 5-10 business day processing time is standard.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt applies a unitary national tax regime without check-the-box elections for LLCs. An Egyptian LLC is a resident entity taxed at the entity level on worldwide income. Hybrid mismatch elections are not generally available; however, thin capitalization and transfer pricing rules apply. Tax consolidation is not permitted for corporate income tax purposes. An LLC may elect to treat certain branches as separate accounting units only for local tax filing convenience, but this does not alter entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (for goods and services, excluding exempt supplies and capital assets). Foreign digital service providers supplying B2B SaaS from outside Egypt are subject to VAT registration and collection obligations regardless of the threshold once making taxable supplies to non-registered customers in Egypt; for B2B supplies, the reverse charge mechanism applies when the recipient is VAT-registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates a real-time e-invoicing and e-receipt system operated by the ETA. All VAT-registered taxpayers must issue invoices through the ETA-approved e-invoice portal or certified integration system, transmitting invoice data to the ETA for fiscal validation and stamping in near-real-time (typically within 24 hours). Foreign e-commerce and SaaS suppliers are required to integrate with the ETA e-invoicing API to issue compliant electronic invoices compliant with the Egyptian schema. Clearance rules require issuance within the statutory timeframe for each supply; failure to transmit or validate invoices triggers fines and suspension of tax clearance certificates.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated for Egyptian VAT, provided the exporter is a VAT-registered taxpayer and holds documentary evidence of the actual export. For B2B SaaS and other digital services, zero-rating applies if the service is exported to a recipient resident outside Egypt, provided the recipient is registered in a foreign jurisdiction and the place of supply is outside Egypt. The taxpayer must show that the intellectual property or digital service is used entirely outside Egypt, and that the export is supported by a written contract, proof of foreign currency payment from overseas, and evidence that the service is not consumed locally.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (via Egypt Customs Authority — Nafeza platform)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (for physical goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate proving receipt of foreign currency export proceeds
Service Agreement or SaaS Subscription Confirmation for exported digital services
ETA-approved export documentation checklist and underlying transfer pricing documentation if applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may audit export zero-rating claims for up to five years. Failure to remit foreign currency within the 180-day deadline or use of ineligible documentation results in disallowance of the zero rate, assessment of VAT at 14% on the full invoice value, plus late payment penalties of 3% per month or fraction thereof (cumulative, capped at 100% of the tax). Fraudulent zero-rating claims (e.g., fake export invoices, overstated foreign remittances) are subject to tax evasion penalties of up to 200% of the evaded tax plus imprisonment penalties under Law No. 67 of 2016 and Law No. 73 of 2022. The ETA also imposes fines for e-invoice non-compliance, between EGP 20,000 and EGP 100,000 per invoice, in addition to clawback of VAT refunds and interest at the statutory rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), operating under Law No. 194 of 2020 on the Central Bank and Banking System and the Foreign Exchange Regulations, Circulars and Executive Instructions issued thereunder; the local unit is the Egyptian Pound (EGP). The CBE is the sole competent authority for exchange-control policy, licensing of banks, operation of the banking file for inward foreign investment and administration of the interbank foreign-exchange market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime under the Articles of Agreement of the CBE and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. Current-account payments, including software-subscription fees paid to an Egyptian pure-play B2B Enterprise SaaS provider, are generally convertibility-friendly and may be settled through local commercial banks using the standard corporate foreign-currency account and SWIFT MT103 infrastructure. Capital-account transactions, such as the initial ISIS of the LLC's registered share capital, direct shareholder loans, and future equity injections, are not unconditionally convertible and require a purpose-clearing submission to the Corporate Banking division of the receiving bank together with supporting corporate registry and, where applicable, GAFI investment approvals. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permitted upon satisfaction of the annual audit requirement, payment or clearance of applicable withholding tax under Article 56 of the Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, submission of the audited financial statements and a notarised board resolution declaring distributable profits. In practice, the CBE may impose documentary verification on the underlying SaaS agreement to distinguish genuine subscription/turnkey income from IP royalty leakage; a fully executed master SaaS terms sheet with merchant-identification, usage volumes and price schedule, together with local tax forms, will materially de-risk the repatriation application.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export proceeds in respect of goods and services, including B2B Enterprise SaaS subscription fees, must be collected in an allowable foreign currency and transferred directly to the exporter's foreign-currency account maintained with an Egyptian bank. For physical goods, the default statutory settlement window is generally the earlier of the contractual credit period or 180 days from the bill of lading/export date unless the CBE grants an explicit extension; for services/software exports, the receivable must be settled within the period specified in the underlying service agreement, which should not exceed one year from the invoice date, and late settlements require bank-level justification. The permanent statutory principle is that 100% of export value must be repatriated to Egypt before a surrender credit is registered. During periodic liquidity-balance interventions the CBE has imposed mandatory conversion ratios (frequently 50% of eligible export proceeds at the prevailing market rate), and the exact percentage in force at the moment of collection must be observed based on the current CBE Circular; the bank will automatically apply the mandatory conversion and credit the corresponding EGP amount to the operational account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium. Egypt does not issue cross-border bank or electronic-money institution (EMI) licences to offshore fintech entities, and a non-resident EMI such as a foreign Wise business account or Stripe Treasury-type wallet cannot independently maintain a domestic EGP settlement account. The legally viable model is indirect: an Egyptian-licensed commercial bank is the master account provider; the foreign EMI is limited to inbound-or-outbound remittance routing via SWIFT or a licensed local payment aggregator (e.g., Paymob or Fawry) under the Payment Systems Regulation Law No. 18 of 2019. Consequently, Stripe Billing and Wise B2B rails can be used only as invoicing/collection front-ends where the actual settlement is redirected to the Egyptian LLC's USD account in a licensed tier-1 bank, or where the transaction size and recurring-subscription model justify integrating with a payments-orchestration partner that has direct the CBE-prudential coverage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence session for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and authorised signatory is generally mandatory at the bank branch in Egypt before account activation, especially when the shareholder files are cross-border and the company has no legacy Egyptian relationship. Certain CBE-regulated banks allow the first interview to be held remotely through a video KYC tool, but standard practice still requires one in-country visit by at least one director or appointed manager for biometric verification and wet-ink specimen signature. Where no director can travel, a notarised power of attorney executed before an Egyptian consulate and accompanied by an apostille/certificate is accepted on a bank-discretionary basis, but a 24–48hour in-branch interview substantially increases deal velocity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner domiciled in a jurisdiction perceived as a tax-haven or under EGMON/Financial Action Task Force monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified colour copies of passports and specimen signature cards; notarised and apostilled company-formation documents of the shareholder; current extract from the shareholder's commercial register; audited financial statements or tax returns of the shareholder for the preceding two years; a board resolution of the shareholder authorising the Egyptian LLC's investment; a completed beneficial-ownership declaration and sanctions-screening self-certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of the initial capital contribution or inbound equity transfer, particularly where the capital amount is disproportionately large relative to projected SaaS operating expenditure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the last 12 months from the remitting institution; an explicit source-of-wealth narrative report; the subscription, share-purchase or share-issue agreement in the LLC's constitutional file; evidence of the corporate purpose and ISIC 6201 activity; and a sworn declaration that the funds derive from lawful software-development and B2B sales invoiced to enterprise customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected circular or round-tripping revenue when B2B SaaS receipts are originated by a customer that also appears as a shareholder or procedural dependence on intra-group software licences.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The full enterprise SaaS master agreement and each order form with addressable nodes/user volumes; remittance-specific invoice/payment reconciliation; customer-side registration and VAT receipts documents; an explanation memorandum on whether any part of the sale is a resale of third-party licences; licence-agreement annexes with the original software publisher if applicable; and independent pricing benchmarks to demonstrate arm's-length charges.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name, nationality, political-affiliation or PEP-status flags generated by sanctions/PEP screening against the directors, shareholders, or authorised signatories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE-compliant independent screening reports essential the use of bank-accepted databases (Dow Jones/Refinitiv/World-Check); judicial-record extracts from country of nationality; attestation by the candidate that they are not a politically exposed person or, if they are, that the source of funds has been identified and verified; and counsel opinion on the absence of any designation by the UN, EU, UK, US OFAC or Egyptian authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of physical economic substance and employment records for the Egyptian LLC, which could demonstrate or façade risk in banking and tax terms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A virtual-office or serviced-office lease agreement covering 24 months; the opening payroll records and social-insurance filings for the planned staff headcount; Ministry of Investment and GAFI establishment certificate; tax registration card with the Egyptian Tax Authority; annual business plan showing the resourcing of software development, professional services and client support in Egypt; and utility/telecom bills or vendor contracts evidencing actual operational continuity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 with the remitter bank exposing the purpose code corresponding to 'direct investment in share capital' or 'resident entity equity'. The Egyptian receiving bank will require the bank's internal foreign-exchange form, a photocopy of the LLC's commercial registry and GAFI investment certificate, a proof of the capital-escrow account if newly formed, and the notarised board minutes accepting the shareholder resolution. To maximise efficiency: (i) instruct the remitting bank to include the LLC's IBAN and the full beneficiary name exactly as registered; (ii) add in Field 70 the reference 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION EG_LLC ISIC-6201' to satisfy automated compliance filtering; (iii) avoid sending mixed purpose amounts in one wire; and (iv) retain the SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation, the currency-conversion advice, and the escrow-to-operational account transfer order as the definitive audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring operating expenses such as cloud-infrastructure, software-license, professional services and marketing outflows, the settlement rail is a standard SWIFT MT103 issued from the LLC's USD operational account directly to the benefit holder, always accompanied by the invoice, the supportive cost-allocation spreadsheet, and a written purpose statement to avoid CBE repersonalisation queries. For one-off or large-ticket technology hardware or infrastructure procurement where a documentary shipment is required, a confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (ICC UCP 600) drawn on a licensed Egyptian issuing bank is available; the transport or service-conformity document package (airway bill / on-premise delivery certificate) and CBE-required paperwork must be presented by the beneficiary before payment. In all outbound instructions, the LLC should use the CBE's accepted Balance of Payments code for 'telecommunications, computer and information services' as the reference, and where the payment could be construed as a dividend, attach the annual GAAP-compliant audit opinion and withholding tax certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable onshore USD/EGP forward contracts executed with an Egyptian licensed bank, with the tenor matched to the underlying SaaS contract-invoice maturities and supported by a written treasury policy;

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in EGP entered with non-resident counterparties or offshore branches of foreign banks, used exclusively to hedge forecast revenue where the onshore market is temporarily illiquid; the hedge must be supported by signed customer subscription agreements and must be marked-to-market in the treasury ledger

Currency swaps between EGP and USD for individual transaction legs limited to known capital-contribution and dividend-repatriation cycles, documented under ISDA or local master agreement and requiring prior CBE/bank treasury confirmation;

Instruments with an embedded optional or corridor structure (e.g., USD/EGP forward-plus or zero-cost collar) only if expressly offered by the onshore bank and permitted under the prevailing CBE circular.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registration renewal and register confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before January 31 immediately following the calendar fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a monthly delinquency surcharge of 10% of the statutory fee; failure to renew for more than 90 days results in suspension of the commercial registration and initiates administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Before April 30 following the calendar fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers tiered penalties from EGP 2,500 to EGP 50,000; late payment surcharge accrues at 1% per calendar month; persistent non-filing results in enforced tax assessment, property seizure, and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and shareholder register amendment confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end, simultaneously with the annual general assembly minutes (due by June 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit annual UBO confirmation and share-transfer amendments exposes the company to AML/CTF fines up to EGP 500,000 and restrictions on legal transactions; prolonged non-compliance enables GAFI to initiate involuntary dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs, irrespective of size or revenue, are legally required to appoint an independent certified auditor at the annual general assembly; there is no minimum turnover exemption
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially converged with IFRS as issued by the Ministry of Finance

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ultimate beneficial ownership must be reviewed and confirmed annually by the board of managers; any shareholding transfer requires prior register amendment filed with GAFI and the Commercial Registry within 14 days of the transfer, and the annual general assembly must ratify the updated UBO schedule
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of General Assemblies and Board Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific statutory tax holiday for ISIC 6201 B2B enterprise SaaS within ordinary Egypt LLC status. A 0% CIT regime is available only to qualifying Free Zone (incl. Suez Canal Economic Zone) entities provided the project exports services outside Egypt and obtains prior ETA/FZA approval; standard LLC SaaS income outside Free Zones is taxed at 22.5%. SME Law 152/2020 permits a presumptive annual tax of 0.5%-1% of turnover for micro/small enterprises with annual revenue not exceeding EGP 20,000,000 in lieu of standard CIT, but this is elective and rarely suitable for enterprise SaaS at scale. Ordinary deductions and the standard 22.5% rate therefore apply in the benchmark case.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian corporate income tax return Form No. 100 (Tax on Profits of Juridical Persons); filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at eta.gov.eg or via the authorised tax agent portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with three mandatory estimated advance CIT payment installments during the tax year; for a calendar-year LLC, prepayments are due by 30 April, 31 July and 31 October.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return and final tax payment are due within four months after the close of the fiscal year. For calendar-year filers, the statutory deadline is 30 April of the following year; nil-return LLCs are still required to file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from enterprise SaaS subscriptions, implementation, training and project management services before deductions and before VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned LLC, enter only revenue economically attributable to the Egyptian entity; SaaS subscription income invoiced through Stripe or Wise must be fully recognised in Egypt and may not be parked offshore without a PE creation analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, including qualifying dividend income received from Egyptian juridical persons under Article 48 participation exemption and government bond interest if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from the Egyptian LLC by a qualifying non-resident corporate parent holding at least 20% for not less than six months may be exempt from Egyptian tax; attach documentary support and holdings computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs and deductible operating expenses such as cloud hosting fees, software development payroll, third-party subcontracting, marketing, lease, utilities, depreciation and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border intercompany expenses must be arm's length, supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; interest, royalties and service fees paid to foreign affiliates and subjected to Egyptian WHT require gross-up analysis and documentary narrative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction schedule identifying all transactions with foreign parent, affiliates, and connected parties, including managed services, cost-sharing, software sub-licensing, debt financing and payment platform charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The TP disclosure form is mandatory for controlled transactions; the Egyptian LLC must state the selected OECD method (CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM or Profit Split) and justify the intercompany pricing of subscriptions and royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before losses and five-year carried-forward tax losses utilised in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned LLC may deduct pre-earned losses only to the extent of 5 carryforward years under Law 91/2005; aggregate carryforward details must be annexed to the electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computed at 22.5%, reduced by estimated prepayments, Egyptian WHT credits and any approved treaty relief; resulting net tax payable or refund carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty reductions cannot be self-assessed; the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a prior ETA treaty approval and the Egyptian LLC must withhold the domestic WHT where applicable. Credit is allowed only for serviceable withholding certificates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers a surcharge of 2% of the tax due for each month or fraction of a month of delay, capped at 50% of the tax; in addition, administrative fines may be imposed by the ETA ranging up to EGP 5,000 per failure. Late payment of assessed tax carries a similar monthly delay surcharge. Persistent non-filing can lead to automatic assessment, criminal liability for tax evasion, and attachment of bank accounts and company assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% default Egyptian dividend withholding tax for non-resident recipients not covered by an exemption. A 0% rate applies to non-resident corporate shareholders that are beneficial owners and qualify for the Article 48 participation exemption by holding at least 20% of the Egyptian LLC's capital or voting rights for a minimum six-month period. Treaty rates for non-qualifying shareholders range from 5% to 15% depending on the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on dividends, interest or royalties, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a current Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the residence state tax authority, legalised or apostilled as applicable and showing the fiscal year and tax ID; (2) complete the ETA treaty benefits application/declaration form before remittance or, at latest, on or before the Egyptian LLC's annual CIT return date; (3) demonstrate beneficial ownership and, for dividend participation relief, provide a shareholder register excerpt proving the 20% holding for the required six-month period; (4) submit the documentation to the ETA competent authority for a formal approval before adopting the reduced or zero rate at source. If WHT was fully or partially applied, a refund application may be filed with the ETA within the statutory limitation window, generally five years, accompanied by the same TRC and supporting evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Egyptian law imposes a 20% withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents and a 20% withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents. Payments for enterprise software license subscriptions and IP exploitation are treated as royalties for WHT purposes. Under Egyptian tax treaties, royalty and interest rates are commonly reduced to 10%-15% (interest may be totally exempt for certain governmental or financial institutions); such relief must be certified by the ETA through the treaty application protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 5,000,000 aggregate annual related-party controlled transactions triggers the mandatory Egyptian Local File and contemporaneous TP study. A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required where the Egyptian LLC belongs to an MNE group with consolidated annual group revenue of at least EGP 2,000,000,000, applying OECD-aligned Egyptian Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply the Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a stand-alone code. However, Egyptian tax law and the ETA apply OECD-aligned substance-over-form principles, judicial anti-abuse doctrine, and the Egyptian GAAR to disregard letterbox companies and deny treaty benefits or intercompany deductions. A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must demonstrate real premises, an active management board, Egyptian payroll, decision-making functions, operational risk control, and sufficient substance to justify its entitlement to Egyptian DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of enterprise SaaS subscription revenue, use of offshore Stripe/Wise or personal bank accounts to divert Egypt-sourced fees without recognition in the Egyptian LLC's accounting records, creation of fictitious invoices, or destruction of books and records to evade CIT and VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will re-assess the full taxable income and impose the outstanding CIT plus the monthly delay surcharge of 2% per month, capped at 50% of the tax; criminal liability under Law 91/2005 carries imprisonment of 3 to 5 years and a fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000, together with confiscation and asset attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts and the ETA may pierce the corporate veil where the LLC is used as a sham. Directors and de facto managers are jointly and personally liable for evaded tax, penalties, and civil restitution; upon initiation of criminal proceedings, travel bans, freezing of bank accounts, and seizure of personal assets of the board members may be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: An Egyptian LLC with no physical office, no employees, no active board resolutions, and all strategic functions or cloud hosting services performed from the non-resident parent or foreign subsidiary, structured solely to minimise corporate tax, shift SaaS profits, or claim treaty benefits without bona fide ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will disregard the Egyptian LLC's personality for CIT purposes, attribute the SaaS revenue to the foreign parent's Egyptian permanent establishment, subject that revenue to 22.5% CIT, disallow intercompany management and royalty deductions, and impose the 10%-20% WHT on deemed profit repatriation; late payment surcharges and penalties are added.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign tax returns for the shell entity may be treated as de facto representatives and held civilly liable for the corporate tax debt; the Egyptian tax execution law permits precautionary travel bans and attachment of directors' personal assets when a company is found to lack real existence and liability is mapped to the controllers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and False Intercompany Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the mandatory transfer pricing disclosure form with the annual CIT return when controlled transactions exceed the threshold, failing to prepare a Local File, or pricing cross-border SaaS licensing, software royalties, cloud costs, management fees, and financing with a profit margin materially different from the arm's length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA will make a transfer pricing adjustment to the Egyptian LLC's taxable income, disallow overstated deductions, recompute CIT at 22.5%, and impose the 2% per month delay surcharge (max 50%). Willful submission of false TP documentation is treated as tax evasion, attracting imprisonment of 3 to 5 years and fines of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who endorse false or non-contemporaneous TP declarations may be prosecuted for abetting tax evasion; the law permits the ETA to collect the additional tax, surcharges, and fines from directors where the LLC is undercapitalised or used as an instrument of the fraud, and to impose asset freezes and travel limitations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting dividends, interest, royalties, or technical fees to a non-resident shareholder or foreign affiliate without deducting and remitting the statutory 10%-20% WHT, or applying DTA zero/reduced rates without a current Tax Residence Certificate, beneficial ownership proof, and formal ETA approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian remitter (LLC) becomes directly liable to pay the WHT not withheld, plus the monthly 2% late-payment surcharge up to a maximum of 50%; the amount can be assessed as a debt against the company and the expense may be disallowed for CIT purposes, increasing the 22.5% tax burden.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute an unlawful remittance without withholding are jointly and severally liable to the ETA for the tax that should have been withheld; tax execution procedure can be directed at the bank accounts and personal assets of the responsible officers, and travel bans are routinely issued for unresolved withholding debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / CFT Breaches Involving B2B SaaS Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting enterprise SaaS payments through Stripe, Wise, or other rails without conducting appropriate customer due diligence, ignoring suspicious transaction reports, accepting third-party funding without ownership verification, or using the Egyptian LLC as a conduit for laundering proceeds of predicate crime through subscription refunds and foreign disbursements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended, attract imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines of up to EGP 10,000,000; money laundering or terrorism-financing related conduct may additionally result in confiscation of funds and accounts, suspension of the entity's commercial licence, and publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated AML compliance officer face personal criminal responsibility, imprisonment, and financial penalties for failing to implement adequate AML controls; assets and bank accounts under their control may be seized, and a travel ban can be imposed pending investigation or trial.
